Overview/Financing labels

Paper 01 · Financing labels

Who Gets the House?

Related-Party Transfers and the Cash–Mortgage Price Gap in New York City

By Pablo LoschiPublic version 3.1Independent document review pending

The question

Buyers who use a mortgage and buyers recorded as paying cash can appear to pay different prices for the same type of home. Is that contrast about financing, or about which people and transactions appear in each group?

The paper uses linked New York City deeds and mortgages, repeat sales, and screens for company buyers and possible related-party transfers. It asks how the price association changes as those transactions are separated.

What the evidence says

The financed-versus-cash contrast for houses is sensitive to transaction composition. In particular, the gap changes when possible same-surname transfers are excluded, and it is small for cash purchases by companies. The paper treats this as an observed association; it does not isolate a causal price premium for mortgage financing or closing certainty.

Validation status

The public version is deposited with replication files. A frozen queue of deed and mortgage instruments still needs two independent blinded readings. The review will measure label error with uncertainty and check whether corrected classifications change the reported estimates.

Until that review and any rerun are complete, the deed and financing classifications remain a material limitation. The current estimates should be read as provisional on those labels.
